title: An asymmetric shock

predict.q: Country B starts at full-employment output (500). World demand for its main export collapses: AD falls by 40. B is in a monetary union; its partners are unaffected. What happens in B in the short run?

options.s: The union central bank cuts B's interest rate, so AD recovers and output stays at 500
options.fb: There is one interest rate for the whole union. It cannot be cut for B alone.

options.s: B's currency depreciates against its partners, so its exports recover and output stays at 500
options.fb: B shares its currency with its partners, so there is no exchange rate between them to fall.

options.s: Output falls to 480 and stays below full employment until B's wages and prices fall
options.fb: Nothing cushions the shock: output 480, price level 90, a gap of 20 until internal devaluation.

options.s: LRAS shifts left to 480, because B's capacity to produce has fallen
options.fb: Demand fell, not capacity. LRAS stays at 500; actual output falls below it.

task: Move the AD-shock slider to −40, then switch between "monetary union" and "own floating currency". Watch output and the price level.

target.do: Move the AD-shock slider to −40 (monetary union), then press Check.

takeaway: Outside the union, a fall in B's currency and interest rate cushions the shock. Inside, B must wait for internal devaluation.
